turns.prompt:
You are given two attached CSV files describing perovskite solar cells as
complete devices — `composition` (absorber), `architecture` (n-i-p =
regular, p-i-n = inverted), `substrate` (glass + transparent electrode),
`etl` (electron-transport layer stack), `htl` (hole-transport layer stack),
`backcontact` (metal / carbon back electrode), `deposition` (absorber
deposition procedure; `>>` separates steps). Each row is a device
CONFIGURATION whose efficiency is the median over at least 2 independently
fabricated cells, so it is a reproducible recipe rather than a single
champion cell:
  - b3_pvk_retention_train.csv: 300 configurations with the measured
    percentage of the initial efficiency still retained at the end of a
    300–1200 h stability test (%).
  - b3_pvk_retention_pool.csv: 100 CANDIDATE configurations whose percentage
    of the initial efficiency still retained at the end of a 300–1200 h
    stability test (%) was NOT measured, columns `candidate_id` and the same
    device columns.

Using the training data, select the 5 candidates with the HIGHEST percentage
of the initial efficiency still retained at the end of a 300–1200 h
stability test (%).

Reason from the device physics — band alignment and selectivity of the
transport layers, interface recombination, contact chemistry and the film
quality the process is likely to give — then end your answer with an
explicit ranked list of candidate_ids, best first, e.g. "Final: c901, c902,
c903, c904, c905".
turns.answer_text:
The training data show that the highest retained efficiencies (typically 94–100 %) cluster around a small number of physically well-motivated design choices: (i) an all-inorganic or low-volatility absorber (CsPbBr, CsPbBrI or carbon-electrode MA/FA perovskites), (ii) a mesoporous TiO2 scaffold that both templates a high-quality film and physically separates the contacts, (iii) omission of a doped organic HTL (especially Spiro-MeOTAD/LiTFSI or acidic PEDOT:PSS) in favour of either no HTL or a chemically inert inorganic/molecular HTL (CuPc, NiMgLiO, SnS, \ldots), and (iv) a carbon back-contact that eliminates metal-ion migration and iodide corrosion.  

These features simultaneously improve band alignment/selectivity, suppress interface recombination and remove the principal chemical degradation pathways (MA deprotonation, Li-hygroscopicity, Ag/Au iodide formation).  

Applying the same criteria to the unlabelled pool immediately isolates five candidates whose stacks are essentially identical to the top-performing training recipes:

- c074 reproduces the CsPbBr / mp-TiO2 / carbon architecture that repeatedly yields 95–98 % retention (Graphene-QDs further passivate the oxide/perovskite interface).  
- c080 and c027 are the classic HTM-free carbon MAPbI cells whose closest training analogues sit at 97 % and 100 %.  
- c052 replaces the oxide HTL with CuPc while retaining the carbon electrode (training analogue 94 %).  
- c096 is the FA analogue of the same carbon stack (training analogue 89 %).  

All other pool entries introduce at least one known degradation channel (Spiro, PEDOT, Ag, pure MA without carbon, ZnO photocatalysis, flexible substrates, \ldots) and are therefore ranked lower.

Final: c074, c080, c027, c052, c096
